Bath and North East Somerset's population increased by around 17,400 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 190,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Bath and North East Somerset increased by 9.9%, from around 176,000 in 2011 to around 193,400 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the South West (7.8%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Bath and North East Somerset was home to around 4.0 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 3.6 in 2011. This area was close to the median population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Bath and North East Somerset than across the South West

Median age in Bath and North East Somerset

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Bath and North East Somerset decreased by one year, from 40 to 39 years of age.

This area had a lower average (median) age than the South West as a whole in 2021 (44 years) and a slightly lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 4,200 (an increase of 13.2%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 2,300 (6.5% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 0.5 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Ethnic groups in Bath and North East Somerset

In 2021, 2.7% of Bath and North East Somerset residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 1.6% in 2011. The 1.1 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South West, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 1.4% to 2.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 92.2% of people in Bath and North East Somerset identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 94.6% in 2011), while 3.3% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 2.6% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 0.8% in 2011 to 1.0% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 2.7% of usual residents in Bath and North East Somerset identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category

Unpaid care in Bath and North East Somerset

In 2021, 4.9% of Bath and North East Somerset residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.5% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.2% in 2011. The proportion of Bath and North East Somerset residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.0% to 2.2%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Bath and North East Somerset (2.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South West (2.8 percentage points, from 7.5% to 4.7%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Bath and North East Somerset decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Religion in Bath and North East Somerset

In 2021, 47.9% of Bath and North East Somerset residents reported having "No religion", making it the most common response in this local authority area (up from 32.7% in 2011). Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South West, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 29.3% to 44.1%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 42.2% of people in Bath and North East Somerset described themselves as Christian (down from 56.5%), while 7.2% did not state their religion (down from 8.5% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 47.9% of usual residents in Bath and North East Somerset reported having "No religion"

Bath and North East Somerset residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 162,500 Bath and North East Somerset residents said they were born in England. This represented 84.0% of the local population. The figure has risen from just under 152,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 86.5% of Bath and North East Somerset's population.

Wales was the next most represented, with just under 4,500 Bath and North East Somerset residents reporting this country of birth (2.3%). This figure was up from just over 4,100 in 2011, which at the time also represented 2.3% of the population of Bath and North East Somerset.

The number of Bath and North East Somerset residents born in Scotland fell from around 2,500 in 2011 (1.4% of the local population) to just under 2,400 in 2021 (1.2%).

In 2021, 84.0% of Bath and North East Somerset residents reported their country of birth as England

Health in Bath and North East Somerset

In 2021, 51.4% of Bath and North East Somerset residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 49.4% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.0% to 33.1%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Bath and North East Somerset residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 0.9%, while those describing their health as "bad" was 3.2% (similar to 2011).

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

In 2021, 0.9% of usual residents said their health was very bad in Bath and North East Somerset

National identity in Bath and North East Somerset

In 2021, 7.6% of Bath and North East Somerset residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 5.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.4%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.9% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Bath and North East Somerset that identified as "British only" increased from 17.8% to 56.3%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK in Bath and North East Somerset (1.9 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South West (1.7 percentage points, from 4.4% to 6.1%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Bath and North East Somerset increased by 1.9 percentage points

Family in Bath and North East Somerset

Of Bath and North East Somerset households, 17.8% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 18.2% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater across the South West (1.2 percentage points, from 19.7% to 18.5%) than in Bath and North East Somerset (0.4 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Bath and North East Somerset decreased by 0.4 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Bath and North East Somerset residents aged 16 years and over, 41.3% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 37.3% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 4 in 10 people (43.4%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 45.9% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Bath and North East Somerset that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership decreased from 8.2% to 8.0%.

This area had the region’s third highest percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership. Across the region, only Bristol (52.8%) and Exeter (48.7%) had a higher percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Bath and North East Somerset increased by 4.0 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Bath and North East Somerset residents aged 16 years and over, 53.0% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 54.7% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.9%) said they were unemployed, compared with 2.4% in 2011. The percentage of retired Bath and North East Somerset residents decreased from 22.2% to 22.1%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed in Bath and North East Somerset (1.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South West (1.6 percentage points, from 56.9% to 55.3%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Bath and North East Somerset decreased by 1.7 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 13.4% of Bath and North East Somerset residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 12.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.4%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 13.0% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 53.6% to 55.2%.

This area had the region’s joint second highest percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week (alongside West Devon). Across the region, only South Hams, with 14.5%, had a higher percentage.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Bath and North East Somerset increased by 0.5 percentage points

Change in housing in Bath and North East Somerset

Of Bath and North East Somerset households, 65.3% owned their home in 2021, down from 66.7% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in five households (19.3%) rented privately, compared with 16.9% in 2011. The percentage of Bath and North East Somerset households that lived in a socially rented property decreased from 14.4% to 14.3%.

The decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home in Bath and North East Somerset (1.5 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South West (1.6 percentage points, from 67.4% to 65.9%). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.0 percentage points, from 63.3% to 61.3%.

The rate of home ownership in Bath and North East Somerset decreased by 1.5 percentage points

Disability in Bath and North East Somerset

In 2021, 6.0% of Bath and North East Somerset residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.2%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.4% in 2011. The proportion of Bath and North East Somerset residents who were not disabled increased from 83.4% to 83.8%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Bath and North East Somerset (1.1 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South West (1.1 percentage points, from 8.1% to 7.0%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Bath and North East Somerset decreased by 1.1 percentage points
